candidate_decisions.reason: Focus kelimesi isim olarak kalırken kaynağın onu anılmayı yükselten adlandırma diye açıklaması ve hemen sonraki âyetteki küçültücü iki adlandırma, hem ad dalını hem yükselme ilişkisini somut bir makro karşıtlık içinde etkinleştiriyor.

Allah adının çağrıldığı odak biçim, 104:2–3'te servetin toplanması ve kalıcılık güvencesi sayılmasıyla karşılaşınca gerçek bağlılığın yönü olarak okunabilir; tapınılan varlık dalı burada servete literal ilahlık yüklemeyen, açıkça analojik bir ilişkiyle etkinleşiyor.

İki merhamet sıfatı, 104:1'de adlandırılan sosyal incitme karşısında hem şefkat ve etkin esirgeme hem de yakın, kalıcı bağ imgesini taşıyor; yakın soy dalı gerçek akrabalık iddiası değil, sınırı açık bir analoji olarak korunuyor.
Merhametin etkin esirgeme yönü, yakın ve kalıcı bağ çağrışımı ile yaşamı taşıyan döl yatağı imgesi; 104:8–9'un mühürlü ve uzatılmış kuşatmasıyla ayrı fakat bütünlüklü bir ters-image ilişkisi kuruyor.
Odaktaki özel adın 104:6'da ateşle birlikte yeniden anılması, merhametli açılışı ve şiddetli hüküm imgesini aynı adlandırılmış ilahî yetkeye bağlayan bağımsız bir bağlam tetikleyicisidir.

Açılıştaki yükseltilmiş adlandırmanın hemen sonraki aşağılama adlarına karşı çerçeve oluşu, cand_cfdd2a8c6dbd4edf6ba7'nin taşıdığı aynı anlam ilişkisidir; kendi B005 dalı ve 104:1 bağlamı o bulguda eksiksiz yer alıyor.

Merhametin yaşamı ve bağı koruyan kuşatıcılığı ile son ayetlerdeki kapalı hapsin karşıtlığı, cand_ca71e15c1849dee89a66 bulgusuyla aynı okumadır; adayın bağlı B001 dalı ve 104:8–9 bağlamı orada korunuyor.

Allah adının ateşle birlikte yeniden görünmesi ve bunun merhamet açılışıyla aynı yetkeye bağlanması, cand_b469a1a4db1a82114353 bulgusuyla tam örtüşüyor; adayın bağlı B001 dalı ve 104:6 tetikleyicisi orada yer alıyor.

Retrospektif notun kalp imgesine ilişkin kısmı, odaktaki merhameti 104:1'deki sosyal incitme ve 104:7'de ateşin kalplere ulaşmasıyla yeni bir içsel boyuta taşıyor. 104:8–9'daki kapanma/döl yatağı karşıtlığı ayrı kuşatma bulgusuyla kapsandığı için bu adaydan çıkarıldı.

context_exclusions.reason: Bu ayet kapanmış kuşatma imgesini verir; adayın burada korunan kalp-okumasına gerekmez ve aynı kapanma ilişkisi macro:nurturing_enclosure_against_confinement bulgusunda taşınır.

candidate_decisions.reason: Yükseltilmiş adlandırmanın hemen ardından gelen küçültücü söz biçimleriyle karşılaştırılması, cand_cfdd2a8c6dbd4edf6ba7 bulgusundaki adlandırma çerçevesinin aynısıdır; bağlı B005 dalı ve 104:1 yüzey tetikleyicisi korunuyor.

Allah adının servetin kalıcılık iddiasından önce bağlılık yönünü belirlemesi, cand_c22cbf440a8252e3610a bulgusundaki aynı makro ilişkidir; adayın bağlı B002 dalı ve 104:2–3 bağlamı o bulguda yer alıyor.

Tekrarlanan merhamet adlarının kusur bulup yayma davranışına karşı şefkat ve esirgemeyi öne alması, cand_dcc1e58a5ad6cf48ccbc bulgusuyla aynı ilişkidir; adayın 104:1 tetikleyicisi ve ilgili odak biçimleri orada korunuyor.

Retrospektif destek, Allah adına güvenin 104:3'teki kalıcılık iddiasıyla karşılaşmasını ve iki merhamet adının 104:4–5'te iki kez anılan kırma imgesiyle karşıtlığını aynı açılış yöneliminin iki ayrı teması olarak birleştiriyor; Allah kök dalı doğrudan bağlamla etkin, merhamet dalı ise paketteki odak biçimlerinden bağımsız biçimde açığa çıkan bir makro sürprizdir.

findings.title: A raised name before words that diminish
findings.claim: The opening's name of Allah is presented as a raised point of reference before 104:1 names people through fault-finding and slander; that order makes the basmala a naming frame against speech that reduces others.
findings.mechanism: The focus word is an ordinary name/designation, and its supplied root account links naming to raising the mention of what is named. The independent trigger is the pair of socially degrading labels in 104:1. Their contact lets the name's raised-designation facet sharpen the opening: the divine name stands as a reference point before the surah introduces speech that lowers people.
findings.reader_payoff: The invocation reads as more than a formula of beginning: its first act of naming establishes a dignifying frame against the social speech that follows.
findings.containment: The focus word still means name, not elevation as a freestanding lexical sense. The sequence supports a contrast in framing; it does not claim that 104:0 explicitly states a social policy or that every act of naming is harmful.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication support and exact focus/context surfaces ground the contrast. Two legacy-unbound walk notes describe its raised-designation effect, so that wider framing remains an attributed contextual inference.

findings.title: The invocation before wealth's promise of permanence
findings.claim: The invocation of Allah precedes the hoarder's claim that wealth has made him enduring, so the opening names the object of devotion before the surah exposes a rival practical reliance.
findings.mechanism: Allah's name is the carrier, with the worshipped-being facet supplying the relation of devotion. The independent trigger is 104:2–3: wealth is gathered and counted, then treated as a source of permanence. The contact between invocation and that permanence claim turns the opening into an orientation of reliance before the later critique appears.
findings.reader_payoff: The basmala becomes an active reorientation of dependence before the surah names wealth as the hoarder's imagined guarantee of lasting life.
findings.containment: The ayat do not call wealth a deity or say that collecting it is literally worship. The comparison is analogical: what is trusted to secure permanence can function as a practical object of dependence.

epistemic.reason: The trusted finding supplies the relation between invocation and wealth as permanence; a legacy-unbound walk articulates the analogical practical-dependence mechanism. The context surfaces ground the trigger, while the analogy remains explicit.

branch_activations.activation: The focus names the object of devotion before the independent context presents wealth as a practical guarantee of endurance. Their contact analogically sharpens the name's devotional direction without turning wealth into a literal deity.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The invocation points reliance toward Allah before the surah exposes reliance on accumulated wealth as permanence.
branch_activations.boundary: No formal worship of wealth is asserted, and the reading does not generalize from the hoarder to every person who owns or counts wealth.

findings.title: Mercy and durable closeness before social injury
findings.claim: The doubled mercy epithets place inward compassion, active care, and a kinship-like closeness before the social injury named in 104:1, making the opening a relational counterpoint to public fault-finding and slander.
findings.mechanism: The two focus forms carry mercy as tenderness that issues in protection and good action; the same root also carries close, durable kinship. The independent trigger is 104:1's attack on people through fault-finding and slander. Contact between these carriers and that hostile social act changes the opening's epithets into a positive relation set against pressure and humiliation.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening's mercy names a way of relating that holds people close and cares for them before the surah shows how speech can push them apart.
findings.containment: The kinship facet is analogical here: 104:1 does not say the people are relatives. The packet supports a relational contrast, not a claim that the focus specifies a biological family or that the later judgment is caused by these particular insults.

epistemic.reason: A trusted publication links the repeated mercy forms with closeness against social pressure. A legacy-unbound walk spells out the anti-pressure mechanism; the kinship image is therefore retained as a bounded contextual analogy.

branch_activations.boundary: This is a contextual contrast, not a claim that the focus explicitly names the later speakers or describes their motives.

findings.title: Mercy as a life-bearing enclosure
findings.claim: The focus's mercy can be heard as care and durable closeness with a life-bearing, womb-like enclosure; the surah's sealed and extended final enclosure becomes its inverse, containment without nurture.
findings.mechanism: The mercy epithets carry active care, while their root also supplies kinship and the womb as separate images of closeness and life held within. The independent trigger is the closing chamber described as sealed in 104:8 and extended in 104:9. Their contact changes the paired epithets from abstract mercy into a protective, life-bearing enclosure against a confinement that only closes in.
findings.reader_payoff: The final enclosure is felt as an inversion of the opening's sheltering care: both contain, but only one holds life and closeness.
findings.containment: The womb, kinship, and confinement relation is an image-level contextual reading. The focus words still name mercy; the ayat do not identify the punishment literally as a womb's opposite or say that the enclosed people lack family ties.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support links the mercy branches with the final enclosure. A legacy-unbound walk supplies the nurturing-container articulation; the focus and 104:8–9 surfaces support the comparison, whose image remains explicitly analogical.

findings.mechanism: The focus carries Allah's distinctive name and the worshipped-being relation. The independent trigger is the same name in the phrase about fire, together with the fire's being kindled. Their exact repetition brings the focus name into contact with the later punitive image, changing the opening from a detached preface into the name of the authority behind both mercy and judgment.
findings.reader_payoff: The fire is read within the same named authority introduced by the mercy epithets, so severity and mercy remain part of one account.
findings.containment: The context directly names the fire as Allah's and says it is kindled. This does not supply a complete account of judgment or assert that the text narrates worship in 104:6.

epistemic.reason: A trusted finding supports the same-name relation, while a legacy-unbound walk attributes the authority reading to the repeated name and fire image. The exact repeated name and fire words ground the contextual link; its broader force stays qualified.

findings.title: Mercy in view of fire reaching the heart
findings.claim: The paired mercy epithets acquire an inward counterpart when 104:7 says the fire reaches hearts: after the social injury named in 104:1, the surah's later image carries the consequence into an inner human seat, making the opening's mercy pertinent at that same depth.
findings.mechanism: The two mercy forms are the carrier of compassion and active care. The independent triggers are the degrading social conduct in 104:1 and the later statement that fire reaches hearts in 104:7. Their ordered contact shifts the opening from an abstract quality to care set against a sequence that moves from social injury toward inward exposure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the opening's mercy matters within this surah: the later fire reaches the heart, not only an external setting.
findings.containment: This is an ordered contrast, not an explicit claim that the particular speakers in 104:1 cause the fire or that 104:0 literally says mercy reaches hearts. The separate sealed-enclosure reading from 104:8–9 is excluded from this bounded finding.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective walk is legacy-unbound, while the focus mercy forms and the supplied 104:1 and 104:7 surfaces support its sequence. The connection remains an inference about the ordered context, not an explicit causal statement.

branch_activations.activation: The social act and the inward destination of the fire are separate contextual cues. Their ordered contact with the focus's active-care branch makes the opening's mercy newly relevant to the interior dimension reached later.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The mercy opening stands in view of the later fire's reach into hearts, giving the sequence an inward as well as social contrast.

findings.title: The opening's name and mercy before permanence and breaking
findings.claim: Two features of the opening take on complementary force in the surah's later context: Allah's name precedes the claim that wealth makes its owner endure, while the paired mercy names answer the repeated name of the breaking place. Together they frame reliance and care before the text exposes imagined permanence and crushing.
findings.mechanism: The Allah name carries the worshipped-referent relation; the independent trigger in 104:3 is the owner's belief that wealth makes him last, which turns the invocation into an orientation of practical dependence. Separately, the two focus mercy forms carry tenderness and active care; the repeated al-hutama in 104:4–5 is an independent breaking image. Contact across these two pairs changes the opening into both a direction for reliance and a counterpoint of care to repeated breaking.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the prefatory invocation as an early orientation: the surah's assurance in wealth and its repeated breaking image arrive after the named source of devotion and the double naming of mercy.
findings.containment: The repeated forms establish contextual contrasts, not a formal causal claim. Wealth is not called a deity, and the focus mercy forms do not literally mean womb or physical protection in this finding.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective reader-walk supplies the two contacts; the wealth permanence statement and repeated breaking word are present in the inline packet. Their integration as complementary opening relations is an attributed, exploratory contextual inference.
